figures.caption: Figure 1. Voltage proﬁles of the all-solid-state half-cells with overcharging: A) SiGr and B) MgSiGr anode at a current density of 1 mA cm−2 and capacity of 1 mAh cm−2. C) Voltage versus time proﬁles (modiﬁed N/P ratio = 0.22).

Figure 2. Cross-sectional SEM-EDS images of the (Mg)SiGr anode after overcharging. Morphologies after overcharging the A) SiGr and B) MgSiGr anodes (modiﬁed N/P ratio = 0.06). In the case of simple SiGr, Li precipitates between the active materials. However, with the underlying Mg layer, the Li is neatly stacked beneath the SiGr active material.

Figure 3. A) Voltage proﬁles of the ﬁrst cycle in the Li plating-stripping test in the half-cell, at a current density of 1 mA cm−2 and capacity of 3.5 mAh cm−2 (modiﬁed N/P ratio = 0.06 at the given current density). B) CEs at a current density of 1 mA cm−2 and diﬀerent capacities. EIS Nyquist plots after cycling with the C) SiGr and D) MgSiGr anodes at a current density of 1 mA cm−2 and a capacity of 1 mAh cm−2 (modiﬁed N/P ratio = 0.22).

Figure 4. Full-cell evaluations of the (Mg)SiGr anodes in pairing with a LiNbO3-coated NCM811 cathode (N/P ratio = 0.15). A) The ﬁrst formation voltage proﬁles of the (Mg)SiGr anodes at a current density of 0.1C (1C = 3.6 mA cm−2). Voltage proﬁles of the B) MgSiGr and C) SiGr anodes during cycling at 0.2C. D) Cycling performance of the corresponding 0.2C (dis)charge evaluation. E,F) The rate capability of the MgSiGr anode at various charging rates and a ﬁxed discharging rate of 0.1C. E) Voltage proﬁles and F) discharging capacities.

Figure 5. X-ray microscopy (XRM) with micro-computed tomography (μ-CT) results of the anode-SE interfaces after the ﬁrst overcharge–discharge cycle. A–C) XRM images of the SiGr anode: A) 3D image at the anode-SE interface, B) pore mapping of the corresponding 3D image, and C) x-y 2D image at the anode-SE interface. D–F) XRM images of the MgSiGr anode: D) 3D image at the anode-SE interface, E) pore mapping of the corresponding 3D image, and F) x-y 2D image at the anode-SE interface.

Figure 6. Full-cell evaluation under practical conditions at room temperature (25 °C) and low stack pressure (3 MPa). Voltage proﬁles of the A) SiGr, B) Li metal (10 μm-thick), and C) MgSiGr anodes at 0.2C for both charge and discharge (N/P ratio = 0.66). D) Cycling performance at 0.2C for both charge and discharge. E) Pouch-cell performance of the MgSiGr full-cell (N/P ratio = 0.6).
Figure 7. Comparative illustration of charging processes in SiGr, Li metal, and MgSiGr anodes.
